author: leoromanovsky
body:
🤖 **Comment from Codex working with Leo:** **Decision [D004, revision 2](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/7894c5971626d9a8b1b146f0368e03bb149e4c65/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/decision-history.md#d004): align Go with the browser's scoped activation-error policy.** Thanks, Aaron — agreed that malformed activation metadata should not break evaluations for customers who have not enabled future-mode opt-out. We settled this in [the browser decision thread](https://github.com/DataDog/openfeature-js-client/pull/423#discussion_r4348001493), implemented at [3704387](https://github.com/DataDog/openfeature-js-client/commit/3704387fc1f33220ffe261539aff59d4e3bb1e6d). You then [confirmed the Node probe and four scope tests](https://github.com/DataDog/openfeature-js-client/pull/423#discussion_r4348262068). **Implemented in [c5fec6a](https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/commit/c5fec6a009ffa29bf53f5377a21856c7c4aa5f56).** Go now parses activation once when configuration arrives, preserves **valid / missing / invalid** states, and consumes the invalid state only for an opted-out subject in `future_experiments_only`. **Shared proofs:** [draft FFE test-data PR #55](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/pull/55) contains the [D004 decision](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/7894c5971626d9a8b1b146f0368e03bb149e4c65/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/decision-history.md#d004), its Lean proof, and the linked validation history.
Behavior — the distinction we are preserving | Situation | Result | | --- | --- | | Opt-out disabled, immediate mode, or no subject cutoff | Bad activation does not introduce an error; retain that mode's normal behavior. | | Future mode + valid subject cutoff + malformed activation | Application default with `PARSE_ERROR` for the affected flag; other valid flags remain usable. | | Future mode + valid subject cutoff + missing/null activation | Skip that exposure-logging allocation and continue to the next allocation. | The deliberate tradeoff is keeping malformed metadata visible when this policy depends on it. For an opted-out future-mode subject, the flag errors even if the malformed allocation is unreachable or an ordinary fallback exists. Your invalid-as-missing proposal would allow that fallback; we're retaining the browser distinction here.
Native validation — local checks at c5fec6a - Full `go test ./openfeature/ -count=1` and `go test -race ./openfeature/ -count=1` pass, including the PR-pinned shared fixtures. - All **90 applicable Lean policy cases** pass through the actual Go configuration decoder and provider. The adapter checks both error codes and selected variants, so returning the default cannot impersonate ordinary fallback delivery. - Regression coverage includes all modes, absent cutoffs, malformed types, unreachable and non-logging allocations, valid neighboring flags, strict `startAt`/`endAt` decoding, and invalid → valid → null → invalid updates through Remote Config and the OpenFeature client. - The new tests fail against the previous all-mode rejection and an invalid-as-missing mutation. An independent review found no remaining issues in the scoped diff and adapter. These are local native checks. Timestamp grammar, the other contract families, CI and system-tests at this new commit remain separate evidence; this update does not claim the other review threads are addressed.
Sneak preview — turning review decisions into reusable, checked SDK contracts The shared decisions and proofs are now published in **[draft FFE test-data PR #55](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/pull/55)** at [7894c59](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/commit/7894c5971626d9a8b1b146f0368e03bb149e4c65). We're building a small “proof” workflow around exactly this kind of cross-SDK review: 1. **[A versioned English decision — D004, revision 2](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/7894c5971626d9a8b1b146f0368e03bb149e4c65/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/decision-history.md#d004)**, linked to where it was set. 2. **[An executable Lean model and checked proof](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/7894c5971626d9a8b1b146f0368e03bb149e4c65/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/lean/Proofs.lean#L22-L26)** of this rule. 3. **[Shared oracle cases](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/7894c5971626d9a8b1b146f0368e03bb149e4c65/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/corpus/browser-proposal.jsonl)** that native SDK adapters can run against pinned source revisions. 4. **[A linked history of evidence](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/7894c5971626d9a8b1b146f0368e03bb149e4c65/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/decision-history.md#historical-linked-checks)**, preserving passing and failing checks separately from the decision's authority. For example, this theorem is checked in the published model: ```lean theorem only_future_cutoff_needs_activation (m : Mode) (a : Attribute) (t : Activation) (logging : Bool) : (policy m a t logging).error = .parseError ↔ m = .future ∧ a = .valid ∧ t = .invalid := by cases m <;> cases a <;> cases t <;> simp [policy, normal] ``` In plain English: within this activation-policy model, `PARSE_ERROR` occurs exactly when future mode, a valid subject cutoff, and invalid activation coincide. Other configuration errors are outside this theorem. The draft prototype passes **36 theorem audits and 313 oracle cases** across the broader opt-out contract. It also checks a concrete counterexample showing that invalid-as-missing and the browser policy differ. The useful result is a reviewable rule that we can carry between PRs, with an evidence trail showing which SDK revision was tested against it. The Lean proof establishes properties of the model. This Go change has separate **[native conformance and regression evidence](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/7894c5971626d9a8b1b146f0368e03bb149e4c65/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/evidence/go-d004/native-receipt.json)**, tied to [c5fec6a](https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/commit/c5fec6a009ffa29bf53f5377a21856c7c4aa5f56). The central PR remains a draft; broader fleet adoption remains a separate decision.
